chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar quoted Muhammad ibn al-Hussein ibn Abil-Khattab, on the authority of Waheeb ibn Hafs, on the authority of Abi Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The cow and the camel suffice for seven people if they gather, whether they are from the same family or not.
ai.seo_question: How many people can share one cow or camel for sacrifice?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Al-Khisal* clarifies the jurisprudential principle that a single cow or camel suffices for seven individuals, regardless of whether they are from the same household or distinct families. It reflects the consensus among Shia jurists regarding the flexibility in sacrificial offerings, emphasizing communal participation in ritual worship. The narration underscores the practical application of Quranic commands on sacrifice, linking domestic and broader social units under one ritual act.
